title: The Persistent Widow
reflectionText: She had no power over the judge, no friend to speak for her — only the same plea, brought again and again until he could not turn her away. Jesus set her beside God himself and asked the harder thing: not whether God will answer, but whether he will find you still asking.
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-24, Batch C (gap CG18). Luke 18:1-8, the Persistent Widow, absent both lanes; distinct from 1539 (Luke 18:9-14, the Pharisee and tax collector). SHORT only. NOTE on shortScripture: per owner direction, shortScripture was NOT used (no committed owner approval for 1584); the WEB short was brought to the honest 300-word floor (WEB 300w, KJV 300w) by giving each stated beat its natural room per ADR-031 — the widow's continual coming (18:3,5) narrated as repetition, the judge's reasoning and the Lord's application (including 18:7 'he bears long with them' and 18:8 'avenge speedily') let to land — with no repeated propositions or invented scene/motive. The 146-word source sits far below 300; if the owner prefers a tighter telling, this is a per-use shortScripture candidate (cf. 1580). Ends on the Son of Man question (18:8).
